notable_absence.finding: The --capella flag's own description says it 'Skips restoring services that are not supported with Capella including: analytics, cluster analytics, bucket query, cluster query, views and users' - but never states which Capella access surface, credential type, or role is needed to perform the restore against the Capella side of the connection. Every RBAC fact on this page (data_backup, analytics_admin, eventing_admin, fts_admin) is a Server role; nothing ties the --capella restore path to any capella-role:* or privilege:capella-* concept, even though the flag exists specifically to target a Capella cluster.

cross_product_finding: The `--capella` flag is a source-page-stated correspondence between this Server-only CLI tool and Capella, which this round's framing otherwise warned against assuming: 'This flag can be used to enable restoring from an on-premise cluster to a Capella one.' Capella does not expose cbbackupmgr as a CLI to its own users, but this page shows the tool is nonetheless usable, from the on-premise side, to push a restore INTO a Capella cluster - with a hard-coded list of services the restore must skip because Capella doesn't support them (analytics, cluster analytics, bucket query, cluster query, views, users). This is a real, narrow, one-directional bridge between the two products' backup worlds, not the general 'same mechanism' correspondence the round's briefing cautioned against assuming.
